_comment: WARROOM-OPSTIMELINE-001 Phase 2 — schedule-side registry for GET /api/ops/timeline and GET /api/ops/cron-today. This is the SCHEDULE side of the join (C6: schedule reads the crontab; execution reads the run-log — never mixed). grace_minutes is deliberately NOT duplicated here — it lives in exactly one place, warroom/jobs.json, and is joined by job_id at query time.
_provenance: A live `crontab -l` read was attempted this pass (read-only, `crontab -l 2>/dev/null | grep -i sasmaster`) and was BLOCKED by this repo's own HOOKS-ENFORCE G10/CRONTAB-INSTALL-GATE-001 hook, which treats any `crontab` invocation as a write attempt regardless of the `-l` flag (a real gate false-positive class, not bypassed — no SASMASTER_GO escape was used for a read). Falling back to two already-committed, cross-cited sources instead of guessing: (1) cron-schedule.html's 'Complete Job Registry' table, a static snapshot dated 2026-04-28 in its own footer ('Sourced from live crontab · Updated 2026-04-28') — STALE, not this session's live truth, used only for jobs it still names; (2) the crontab-derived display names already rendered in warroom-v5.html's static Cron Today sidebar (lines 697-704, pre-this-card) and buildTimeline()'s TL array (lines 3054-3060, pre-this-card) — both of which are themselves artifacts of an earlier human capture of the real crontab, and both of which THIS CARD replaces with a live-computed render.
_filename_resolution: The two grey Cron Today entries the card names ('sync to s3 cache.sh', 'process jobs.sh') are SPACED display names, not real filenames — generate-status.js's parseCrontab() (line 655) derives display name as `name.replace(/-/g, ' ')` from either a `# comment` or the matched `<script>.sh` filename (line 637's scriptMatch regex). Applying that same deterministic transform in reverse against the two spaced names yields the on-disk filenames sync-to-s3-cache.sh and process-jobs.sh — confirmed by code derivation (generate-status.js:637-655, cited exactly), not assumed hyphenation. generate-status.js:1001's own comment independently corroborates 'sync-to-s3-cache.sh' by that exact hyphenated name. process-jobs.sh has no independent second citation in this repo this pass — flagged as derived-not-doubly-confirmed.
_cadence_note: expected_cadence_seconds for the two infra-only entries above (and the other infra crons below) is the INTERVAL implied by the cron field pattern already rendered in the pre-existing static markup (`*:*/5` etc.) — real information (that pattern itself came from a human crontab capture), but the exact minute-anchor within the hour is NOT independently confirmed this pass (cadence×N repeats-per-day, not a single scheduled_at). expected_cadence_seconds is null wherever no such pattern exists.
_grace_join_note: grace_job_id is the exact key into warroom/jobs.json's `jobs.*.job_id` this row joins against for its grace window (C6: one source, joined, not copied). null means warroom/jobs.json has no row for this job at all — such a row is ALWAYS grace_unset when its slot elapses with no matching run, same outcome as an UNSET value, since neither state is knowable. IMPORTANT COLLISION FLAGGED, not silently resolved: warroom/jobs.json's job_id 'daily-visuals' names the CANVAS-tab regenerate-artifact dispatch target ('CANVAS Daily Visuals', a 501 stub, exec 'NOT BUILT'), NOT the cron job scripts/daily-visuals.sh below ('board + arch PNGs', cron 2 5 * * *) — two different jobs that happen to share a job_id string across the two registries. This row's grace_job_id is therefore deliberately left null (not 'daily-visuals') to avoid silently borrowing the wrong entity's grace window.
